titulo: What Could Have Happened? Phrasal Verbs and Scientific Discoveries in Biology
titulo_es: ¿Qué habría pasado? Phrasal verbs y descubrimientos en biología
estandares: Analizo hechos pasados y sus posibles alternativas. Comprendo textos divulgativos sobre avances científicos y discuto sus implicaciones éticas.
competencias: Construir el tercer condicional para hablar de lo que no ocurrió; usar phrasal verbs frecuentes; comprender y explicar avances en biología y bioética; escribir y decir fechas correctamente.
componentes: Pensamiento crítico, comunicación, colaboración y creatividad.

proyecto.descripcion_es: En parejas, los estudiantes eligen un descubrimiento biológico (la penicilina, el ADN, las vacunas) y presentan qué habría pasado si no se hubiera dado, usando el tercer condicional y al menos ocho phrasal verbs.
proyecto.descripcion_en: In pairs, students choose a biological discovery (penicillin, DNA, vaccines) and present what would have happened if it had never occurred, using the third conditional and at least eight phrasal verbs.

lecciones.content_es:
Lo que no pasó

Sirve para imaginar un pasado distinto al real: If Fleming hadn't left the plate uncovered, he wouldn't have discovered penicillin.

La fórmula

If + past perfect (had + participio), would have + participio.

  • If I had studied, I would have passed. (no estudié y no pasé)
  • If they had left earlier, they wouldn't have missed the flight.

Contracciones

If I'd known, I'd have told you. — el primer 'd es had y el segundo es would.

Errores frecuentes

  • Después de if nunca va would: If I would have known es incorrecto.
  • Se dice would have, no would of, aunque suenen igual.
lecciones.content_en:
What did not happen

It imagines a past different from the real one: If Fleming hadn't left the plate uncovered, he wouldn't have discovered penicillin.

The formula

If + past perfect (had + participle), would have + participle.

  • If I had studied, I would have passed. (I did not study and I did not pass)
  • If they had left earlier, they wouldn't have missed the flight.

Contractions

If I'd known, I'd have told you. — the first 'd is had and the second is would.

Common mistakes

  • After if there is never would: If I would have known is wrong.
  • It is would have, not would of, even though they sound alike.

lecciones.t: Modales perfectos: would have, could have, should have
lecciones.t_en: Perfect modals: would have, could have, should have
lecciones.content_es:
Hablar del pasado que no fue

Todos siguen la fórmula modal + have + participio.

  • would have – lo que habría pasado: I would have gone, but I was sick.
  • could have – lo que era posible y no se hizo: You could have asked for help.
  • should have – reproche o arrepentimiento: I should have studied more.
  • might have / may have – suposición sobre el pasado: He might have forgotten.
  • must have – deducción casi segura: She must have left early.
  • can't have – deducción negativa: He can't have finished so fast.

Ojo

El modal nunca cambia y el verbo siempre va en participio, no en pasado simple: should have gone, no should have went.
lecciones.content_en:
Talking about the past that never was

They all follow the formula modal + have + participle.

  • would have – what would have happened: I would have gone, but I was sick.
  • could have – what was possible but was not done: You could have asked for help.
  • should have – reproach or regret: I should have studied more.
  • might have / may have – a guess about the past: He might have forgotten.
  • must have – near-certain deduction: She must have left early.
  • can't have – negative deduction: He can't have finished so fast.

Careful

The modal never changes and the verb is always a participle, not a simple past: should have gone, not should have went.

lecciones.content_es:
Qué son

Un verbo + una partícula (preposición o adverbio) que juntos significan algo distinto: look es mirar, pero look after es cuidar.

Separables e inseparables

  • Separables: el objeto puede ir en medio. Turn on the light = Turn the light on. Si el objeto es un pronombre, va obligatoriamente en medio: Turn it on, nunca turn on it.
  • Inseparables: la partícula no se separa. Look after the baby, no look the baby after.

Con tres palabras

look forward to, get along with, come up with, run out of — nunca se separan.

Consejo

No traduzcas la partícula por separado: memoriza el phrasal verb completo con un ejemplo.
lecciones.content_en:
What they are

A verb + a particle (preposition or adverb) that together mean something different: look is to watch, but look after is to take care of.

Separable and inseparable

  • Separable: the object can go in the middle. Turn on the light = Turn the light on. If the object is a pronoun, it must go in the middle: Turn it on, never turn on it.
  • Inseparable: the particle never separates. Look after the baby, not look the baby after.

Three-word ones

look forward to, get along with, come up with, run out of — they never separate.

Advice

Do not translate the particle on its own: memorize the whole phrasal verb with an example.

lecciones.t: Phrasal verbs de estudio e investigación
lecciones.t_en: Phrasal verbs for study and research
lecciones.content_es:
Investigar y aprender

  • look up – buscar un dato: Look up the word in the dictionary.
  • find out – descubrir información: Scientists found out that…
  • figure out – deducir, resolver: We figured out the pattern.
  • point out – señalar: The article points out a risk.
  • carry out – llevar a cabo: They carried out an experiment.
  • bring about – provocar un cambio: The discovery brought about a revolution.

Proceso y resultado

  • go over – repasar · write down – anotar
  • give up – rendirse · keep on – seguir insistiendo
  • turn out – resultar ser: It turned out to be harmless.
  • rule out – descartar: They ruled out the other hypothesis.
lecciones.content_en:
Researching and learning

  • look up – to search for a piece of information: Look up the word in the dictionary.
  • find out – to discover information: Scientists found out that…
  • figure out – to work out, to solve: We figured out the pattern.
  • point out – to indicate: The article points out a risk.
  • carry out – to perform: They carried out an experiment.
  • bring about – to cause a change: The discovery brought about a revolution.

Process and result

  • go over – to review · write down – to note
  • give up – to quit · keep on – to persist
  • turn out – to prove to be: It turned out to be harmless.
  • rule out – to discard: They ruled out the other hypothesis.

El método científico

Bioética

lecciones.t: La fecha: días, meses y números
lecciones.t_en: The date: days, months and numbers
lecciones.content_es:
Escribir la fecha

  • Americano: month/day/year — 03/15/2026 = March 15, 2026
  • Británico: day/month/year — 15/03/2026 = 15 March 2026

Por eso, en textos internacionales conviene escribir el mes con letras para evitar confusiones.

Decirla

March the fifteenth, twenty twenty-six o the fifteenth of March.

Ordinales que cambian

1st first, 2nd second, 3rd third, 5th fifth, 8th eighth, 9th ninth, 12th twelfth, 20th twentieth, 21st twenty-first.

Preposiciones

on Monday, on March 15th · in March, in 2026 · at the weekend, at Christmas.

Días y meses siempre con mayúscula inicial.
lecciones.content_en:
Writing the date

  • American: month/day/year — 03/15/2026 = March 15, 2026
  • British: day/month/year — 15/03/2026 = 15 March 2026

That is why in international texts it is safer to write the month in words.

Saying it

March the fifteenth, twenty twenty-six or the fifteenth of March.

Ordinals that change spelling

1st first, 2nd second, 3rd third, 5th fifth, 8th eighth, 9th ninth, 12th twelfth, 20th twentieth, 21st twenty-first.

Prepositions

on Monday, on March 15th · in March, in 2026 · at the weekend, at Christmas.

Days and months are always capitalized.

repaso.resumen_es:
Lo esencial del periodo

El tercer condicional y los modales perfectos comparten la misma pieza: have + participio. Sirven para hablar de un pasado que no ocurrió, para lamentarlo o para deducir qué pasó. Los phrasal verbs son la otra mitad del periodo.

Puntos gramaticales

  • If + had + participio, would have + participio.
  • should have (arrepentimiento), could have (posibilidad no usada), must have (deducción), can't have (deducción negativa).
  • Nunca would of; siempre would have.
  • Phrasal verbs separables: con pronombre, el objeto va en medio (turn it on).

Vocabulario

Phrasal verbs de investigación (carry out, find out, rule out, turn out), léxico de biología y bioética, y la fecha en formato americano y británico.
repaso.resumen_en:
The core of the term

The third conditional and perfect modals share the same piece: have + participle. They talk about a past that did not happen, regret it or deduce what happened. Phrasal verbs are the other half of the term.

Grammar points

  • If + had + participle, would have + participle.
  • should have (regret), could have (unused possibility), must have (deduction), can't have (negative deduction).
  • Never would of; always would have.
  • Separable phrasal verbs: with a pronoun the object goes in the middle (turn it on).

Vocabulary

Research phrasal verbs (carry out, find out, rule out, turn out), biology and bioethics vocabulary, and the date in American and British format.
